Question: What physical and orbital characteristics (such as absolute magnitude, estimated diameter, and velocity) are the strongest indicators of whether a near-Earth asteroid is classified as potentially hazardous?

Variables that might be related:
- Miss distance
- Size (diameter)
- Velocity

https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sunethjayawardana/nasa-near-earth-objects-neo-full-dataset

• Near-Earth Objects (NEOs): Any asteroid or comet that comes within 1.3 AU of the Sun.
• Potentially Hazardous Asteroids (PHAs): A specific subset of NEOs that pose a more significant threat. To be classified as a PHA, the asteroid must:
	- Come within 0.05 AU of Earth (about 4.6 million miles or 7.5 million kilometers).
	- Be large enough to cause significant regional damage (typically larger than 140 meters or 460 feet in diameter).

